steps.body: A **parallelogram** slices a triangle off one side and reattaches it to the other, forming a rectangle of the SAME base and height — no halving needed. Area = **base × height**: base 6, height 4 gives 6 × 4 = **24**. Unlike a triangle, a parallelogram is already the full rectangle in disguise.

widget.prompt: A parallelogram has base 9 and height 5. What is its area?

choices.label: 22.5 square units
choices.feedback: 22.5 applies the TRIANGLE's ×1/2 — but a parallelogram is the full rectangle, no halving: 9 × 5 = 45.

predict.prompt: A parallelogram with base 9 and height 5 — same base and height as a 9 × 5 rectangle. Its area will be…

options.label: Exactly the rectangle's — the slant doesn't cost area
Half — slanted shapes take the ½ like triangles

predict.reveal: Slice the overhanging triangle off one end and slide it to the other: the parallelogram reassembles into the 9 × 5 rectangle exactly, so the area is the full 45. The ½ belongs to triangles alone — a parallelogram is two of them.

explanationVariants: A parallelogram doesn't halve like a triangle — it's already rectangle-equivalent: 6 × 4 = 24.
Cutting and reattaching a triangle piece turns the parallelogram into a full rectangle of the same area.

widget.prompt: A parallelogram has base 6 and height 4. Which is its area?

choices.label: 24 — base times height, no halving
choices.feedback: Right — a parallelogram equals a rectangle of the same base and height: 6 × 4 = 24.

choices.label: 12 — half of base times height, like a triangle
choices.feedback: That's the TRIANGLE rule. A parallelogram doesn't halve — it's already rectangle-shaped when rearranged: 24.

choices.label: 10 — base plus height
choices.feedback: Area multiplies, it doesn't add. Base × height = 6 × 4 = 24.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Right — a parallelogram equals a rectangle of the same base and height: 6 × 4 = 24.
widget.successFeedback: Right — a parallelogram equals a rectangle of the same base and height: 6 × 4 = 24.

steps.body: A **trapezoid** has two parallel bases of DIFFERENT lengths. Split it diagonally into two triangles — one using the long base (b1), one the short base (b2), both sharing the height. Adding those triangle areas gives the formula: **1/2 × (b1 + b2) × height**. Average the two bases, then apply the triangle rule.

explanationVariants: Add the bases (12), take half the height times that sum: 18.

widget.prompt: A trapezoid has bases 8 and 4, and height 3. What is its area?

choices.label: 12 square units
choices.feedback: 12 uses only the LONG base (8) with the triangle rule (1/2 × 8 × 3), ignoring the short base entirely. Average both: 1/2 × (8+4) × 3 = 18.

choices.label: 96 square units
choices.feedback: 96 multiplies all three numbers together (8×4×3) without the 1/2 or the averaging. The formula is 1/2 × (8+4) × 3 = 18.

widget.prompt: A trapezoid has bases 10 and 6, height 4. Using the two-triangle decomposition: triangle 1 (base 10) has area 1/2×10×4=20. What is triangle 2's area (base 6)?

choices.label: 20 square units
choices.feedback: 20 repeats triangle 1's area. Triangle 2 uses the OTHER base (6): 1/2 × 6 × 4 = 12.

explanationVariants: Both methods agree: decomposition and the formula give the same 32.

widget.prompt: Triangle 1 has area 20 and triangle 2 has area 12 (same trapezoid as before). What is the trapezoid's total area?

choices.label: 8 square units
choices.feedback: 8 subtracts instead of adding the two triangle pieces. Together they make the whole trapezoid: 20 + 12 = 32.

choices.label: 240 square units
choices.feedback: 240 multiplies the two areas. Combining two pieces of a shape means ADDING: 20 + 12 = 32.

hints: A trapezoid has two DIFFERENT-length parallel bases.
explanationVariants: Average the bases (10), multiply by height (5): 50.

widget.prompt: A trapezoid has bases 14 and 6, and height 5. What is its area?

choices.label: 70 square units
choices.feedback: 70 uses only the long base (14) with a parallelogram-style rule (14 × 5), ignoring the short base. Average both bases first: 1/2 × (14+6) × 5 = 50.

choices.label: 35 square units
choices.feedback: 35 uses only the long base with the TRIANGLE rule (1/2 × 14 × 5), missing the short base's contribution. Average both bases: 1/2 × 20 × 5 = 50.

steps.body: Three shapes, three rules built on triangles.
takeaways: Parallelogram area = base × height — no halving, it's rectangle-equivalent.
Trapezoid area = 1/2 × (base1 + base2) × height — average the bases, then apply the triangle rule.
Every formula traces back to decomposing the shape into triangles or rectangles.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Parallelogram: base × height, no half. Trapezoid: average the two bases, then use the triangle rule.** For bases 6 and 2, height 4: 1/2 × (6+2) × 4 = 16.

widget.prompt: A trapezoid has bases 6 and 2, height 4. What is its area?

choices.label: 12 square units
choices.feedback: 12 uses only the long base (6) with the triangle rule, ignoring the 2. Average both: 1/2 × (6+2) × 4 = 16.

choices.label: 32 square units
choices.feedback: 32 skips the 1/2 entirely ((6+2) × 4 = 32 without halving). The formula is 1/2 × (6+2) × 4 = 16.
